subject.title: feat(codex): add leased remote supervision takeover

question: Should exact remote takeover require a new Codex App Server-owned fenced lease shared by Desktop, CLI, and OpenClaw, or may OpenClaw rely on a node-local lease that independent native clients do not enforce?
rationale: Current Codex supports multi-connection rejoin and connection-scoped approval traffic but exposes no exclusive ownership primitive, so authority, fencing, and recovery semantics require explicit cross-project maintainer intent.

options.title: Require Codex-owned lease
options.body: Coordinate an upstream fenced ownership and approval-handoff contract before enabling paired-node continuation or archive.

options.title: Accept node-local lease
options.body: Let the paired OpenClaw node arbitrate ownership while accepting that unmodified Desktop and CLI clients are not authoritatively fenced.

options.title: Keep remote read-only
options.body: Retain metadata discovery and local snapshot branching until a shared native ownership contract exists.

recommendation.title: Require Codex-owned lease
recommendation.body: Coordinate an upstream fenced ownership and approval-handoff contract before enabling paired-node continuation or archive.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged supervision design and this follow-up issue make this person the strongest current OpenClaw routing candidate for the cross-project decision.
